messages.author: d468156386723bfa
messages.subject: distsamp densities
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to analyze data that I have obtained from conducting
line transect surveys. I modeled detectability in DISTANCE to come up
with density estimates, and am now trying to use distsamp to examine
some the covariates that the candidate models in DISTANCE deemed
important, in terms of their relationship with density and/or
detection. I have about 2019 km of survey effort and have enough
detections for each of the three habitat strata that I am interested
in. I also have observer, and 2 continuous habitat variables that I
have included in the analysis.

The problem is that my densities are very, very high compared to what
I got in DISTANCE. While I am more concerned with examining the
covariates in the context of density vs. detection than with the
overall density estimate, it is unsettling that the estimates are so
high. The detections are entered as clusters so I was wondering if
that may be the problem. I only included strata with enough
detections (removed those that are not suitable habitat), but there
still are a lot of zero detections. I do have a spike of detections
about 60m from the line that I thought may be the problem (although it
seemed to work in DISTANCE), so just to experiment I truncated
distances out to that spike and still got very high densities. Any
suggestions would be greatly appreciated. Here is the general null
code that I used and the results. Other models with covariates had
similar estimates.

(fm1 <- distsamp(~ 1 ~ 1, ltUMF, unitsOut="kmsq"))

Call:
distsamp(formula = ~1 ~ 1, data = ltUMF, unitsOut = "kmsq")

Density:
Estimate SE z P(>|z|)
5.59 0.00414 1350 0

Detection:
Estimate SE z P(>|z|)
4.39 0.00267 1647 0

AIC: 556243.6


Backtransformed linear combination(s) of Density estimate(s)

Estimate SE LinComb (Intercept)
267 1.11 5.59 1



Thanks,

Matt

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] distsamp densities
parts:
Hi Matt,

It's hard to know if your density estimates are unreasonable without more information. What is the study species? How many transects did you run? What was the "naive" density estimate (detections/sample area)? How did you treat the clusters? It would be helpful to see the results of:

head(ltUMF)
summary(ltUMF)
summary(fm1)

We test all the model fitting functions on simulated data so I don't think there is a problem with distsamp, but it is always possible that the estimates represent a local minima in the likelihood function instead of the global minima. Perhaps you could try different starting values, eg

distsamp(~1 ~1, ltUMF, starts=c(2, 10))


Richard

parts:
Richard,

Thanks for the response.
The study species are Wilson’s snipe. We ran 1127 line transects
(1.8 km in length). The naïve density is appx. 3.06 individuals per
kmsq (about 1.9 clusters per kmsq). About 60 percent of the
detections were single individuals, and by far most detections were in
small clusters (<5 indv), with a few exceptions of concentrated
birds. So, the estimates of >200 certainly do not make sense.
The study was done in transects but line lengths are broken down by
the length of each habitat encountered and the subsequent habitat
specific covariates (that’s why it lists over 5000 sites). I used the
distance cut points assigned by DISTANCE from my top model and they
are at intervals of 7meters, out to 218 meters.
I am quite certain it is operator error on my part and no fault of
distsamp. I am pretty new at this. Thanks.

Here are some more details….

After using the starting values (2,10) the density parameter estimate
decreased substantially, but detection is still quite high and the

had similar results.

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] distsamp densities
parts:
hi Matt,
 
 I can think of two things that could be cause for the difference. First, what exactly was the distance function used in DISTANCE?  You should rerun the DISTANCE analysis with precisely the same distance function and see how the results compare.  

 Are DISTANCE and distsamp() treating the clusters differently?  If you're inputting the cluster as the basic observation in both then the results should be comparable.

regards,
andy
